title: Pull-Up
summary: Pull your bodyweight up to a bar with an overhand grip: lats are the main mover, with biceps and mid-back helping and a big stretch at the hang.

muscles.why: The lats pull the upper arm down and back toward the body (shoulder adduction and extension). From a dead hang they start fully stretched.
The elbow flexors bend the elbow against bodyweight; overhand grip gives the biceps a little less leverage than palms up (0.6 vs 0.8 for the chin-up).
Rhomboids and mid traps pull the shoulder blades down and back near the top.
The rear delts help extend the shoulder: minor.
You hold your bodyweight (swap tag 'More grip demand').

setup.text: Grip a little wider than your shoulders, palms facing away.
Start from a dead hang with straight arms.
Cross your ankles or keep the legs slightly in front to stop swinging.

form_cues.why: Starting the pull from the shoulders sets the shoulder blades first.

form_cues.cue: Drive the elbows toward your ribs
form_cues.why: Elbows toward the ribs is the lat's line of pull.

form_cues.cue: Get your chin over the bar
form_cues.why: Chin over the bar finishes the range.

form_cues.cue: Use the full range. The dead hang at the bottom is the stretch that builds the lats.
form_cues.why: The dead hang is where the lats are longest.

form_cues.cue: Lower all the way, every rep

bias_tweaks.effect: Coaches use it for 'width' (upper lats and teres major); the lat is one muscle, so this is a tendency.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Pulldown EMG was similar across grip widths, and the wide grip allowed less load.

bias_tweaks.effect: More biceps help; most people get more reps.
bias_tweaks.caveat: Lat EMG was a little higher with an overhand grip in pulldowns; activity, not growth.

bias_tweaks.effect: More time in the stretch per rep; also a way to progress before you can add load.

mistakes.text: Kipping or swinging to finish reps.
mistakes.fix: Use strict reps; if you can't, use bands or the assisted machine.

mistakes.text: Half reps that never reach a full hang.
mistakes.fix: Straighten the arms at the bottom every rep.

mistakes.text: Craning the neck to get the chin over.
mistakes.fix: Pull the chest toward the bar instead.

misconceptions.myth: Wide-grip pull-ups are best for lat width.
misconceptions.reality: Lat EMG barely changes with grip width; width focus is a coaching model, not a measured result.

misconceptions.myth: You need to do pull-ups before you can build a back.
misconceptions.reality: Pulldowns train the same muscles and let you progress in small steps.

lower_risk.text: When you add load, the app suggests one bodyweight-only set of 5 first (assisted machines: one set with one step more assistance). Without added load the first working set is its own warm-up.
The app counts your effective load (bodyweight share plus added load) and suggests more weight only when the jump is 5% or less; otherwise it adds a rep first, up to 2 past the top of the range.
Aim for about 3 reps in reserve in the 6-10 rep range. Stop when you can't reach the bar without kipping; assistance or a band lets you keep training close to failure.
Lower under control to a full hang; don't drop into it.
If the full hang doesn't feel right for your shoulders, use the range and grip you can train comfortably.

alternatives.why: Same movement with machine assistance, so you can train in the target rep range.
Same pull, seated, any load you need.

alternatives.goal_label: Home gym: no equipment / bar only

notes: Lat findings by grip are EMG only.
Ratings and display bands are the library model (main >= 0.75, helper 0.4 to < 0.75, minor 0.25 to < 0.4, not counted < 0.25).
Technique and load management only. This page makes no medical or injury claims.
